I'm helping a small business migrate over to Google Apps for Work. For those unaware, this is the paid version of Google services that provides (amongst other things) Administrator control.

I'm confused as to whether either of the two paid-tiers will give us an email address at our chosen domain (e.g. john.smith@mycompany.com). The website indicates it WILL, however, in other administrator documentation it speaks only to tying into existing domains that are already owned. To be more specific, this company I'm involved with does not own any domain names; they are only interested in having a Google email address with a custom domain name. I am fairly confident that this feature is included in both Google Apps for Work packages, but am looking for some verification before I move forward. Any insight is much appreciated.

EDIT: Here's a [LINK ](https://apps.google.com/pricing.html)to an explanation of the GAPPs for Work tiers

And here's a [LINK ](https://apps.google.com/products/gmail/)that further suggests that a custom email address is included
Anybody use Google Apps for Work? If so, I've got some questions
You need to buy the domain and update the MX records for that domain to point to google's mail servers. You could also use google domains as your registrar, but any domain registrar would work.

Ok so I went through something similar myself recently.

GAFW did not use to include a domain, and it doesn't even integrate well with their own domain purchasing system Google Domains. GAFW will simply point you at a partner service like WIX (at least it did a few months ago).

You are far better off just buying a domain from a dedicated registrar like GoDaddy and then making the few simple record changes needed to prove ownership of the domain when registering the GAFW account. This will leave you with a custom domain based email managed by Google with admin controls and all of that. The advantage is that you own the domain somewhere where it is portable and has many more control options.

EDIT - It does look like the package has been updated to include a custom domain in the price, but that just likely means they have partnered with a random registrar and will buy it FOR you which tends to leave you with less management options than buying the domain directly from a registrar yourself (MS Office 365 has a similar option). Or they have integrated Google Domains a little further now but last I looked it wasn't very feature rich compared to established registrar services
